title.en: To the Tune Qingyu’an: The Lantern Festival

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource. Lines broken at the punctuation for reading; text unchanged.
edition.zh: 据维基文库。按标点分行，文字未改。

basis.en: Song dynasty lyric (ci); the author died in 1207.

note.en: The Lantern Festival, the fifteenth night of the first month, filled Song cities with lamps, and Xin Qiji spends most of the lyric on the noise and glitter. Then he finds the person he was looking for standing apart, where the lanterns are few. The scholar Wang Guowei later took these last lines as the third and highest stage of any great undertaking: after long searching, you turn, and it is there.
note.zh: 元宵是正月十五之夜，宋代城市里灯火满街，辛弃疾用大半篇幅写那热闹与辉煌。然后，他要找的那个人站在一旁，在灯火稀疏的地方。后来王国维把这几句当作成就大事业、大学问的第三重、也是最高的境界：千百度寻找之后，蓦然回首，它就在那里。

excerpt.orig: 眾裡尋他千百度；驀然回首，那人卻在，燈火闌珊處。
excerpt.en: In the crowd I looked for that one a thousand times; / then suddenly I turned my head, / and that one was there, / where the lamplight was thin.
excerpt.zh: 众里寻他千百度；蓦然回首，那人却在，灯火阑珊处。

gloss.en: A thousand trees in flower: the lanterns of the Lantern Festival, the fifteenth night of the first month, hung on every tree.
gloss.zh: 花千树：形容元宵节（正月十五）灯火之多，像千树花开。

gloss.en: Fireworks falling like a rain of stars.
gloss.zh: 星如雨：指焰火纷纷，乱落如雨。

gloss.en: Jade pot: the moon, or a lantern of white jade.
gloss.zh: 玉壶：比喻明月；一说指白玉制成的灯。

gloss.en: Lanterns shaped like fish and dragons, danced through the streets.
gloss.zh: 鱼龙舞：舞动鱼形、龙形的彩灯。

gloss.en: Moth-shaped pins, snow willows and gold threads: the ornaments women wore in their hair on festival night.
gloss.zh: 蛾儿、雪柳、黄金缕：都是古代妇女元宵节戴在头上的装饰品。

gloss.en: Thin, fading, few: where the lamps give out.
